objections.objection: The thread itself says the specific change is not detailed, while the hypothesis lists several distinct mechanisms (per-CG level reset, GRT not modeling DRT taper, GPL NDR unawareness), so the citation cannot establish which cause was fixed or whether the congestion mechanism was actually the one changed.

objections.claim_attacked: observation/title: GRT overflow/timeout is treated as routing congestion caused by CTS NDR level policy
objections.objection: The record reports GRT being overly cautious and high overflow counts causing timeout, but gives no DRT DRC count, no before/after congestion map, and no separation between a real upper-layer clock congestion problem and a GRT cost-model artifact; 'routing congestion' is therefore stronger than the shown evidence.

mechanism_check: N-D — a bare reference to PR #11136 could plausibly implement one of the listed candidates, but the record does not say whether it changed level definition, GRT behavior, or GPL awareness, so the intervention-to-outcome mechanism is not determinable from this thread.
evidence_check: ASSERT — the only post-state is closure as completed via #11136, with no post-fix skew, congestion, overflow, runtime, or test-outcome measurement.
attribution_check: SUPPORTS — the direct quote carries jfgava, a 2026-08-19 date, and the issue locator, and it supports the narrow claim that the issue was closed with a reference to #11136, though not the content or efficacy of that PR.
missing_from_story: The actual PR #11136 description/diff and which candidate was implemented
Whether the fix changed global level depth across gated clocks, applied root-only NDRs, enabled soft NDR during GRT, modeled DRT taper in GRT, or made GPL NDR-aware
Before/after skew, clock wirelength, congestion/overflow, runtime, and timeout status for mempool_group, ca53, and ibex
DRT DRC results or proof that GRT overflow was not merely an overestimate
The outcome of jfgava's planned tests
Which clock-tree levels received 2s1w NDRs and how gated-clock roots were re-leveled after the fix
most_defensible_part: The concrete prior-state mechanism is the strongest part: NDRs are applied only to the first half of clock-tree levels, leaves are ignored, and CTS treats each gated clock as its own builder with the gated clock root at level 0, which is a coherent reason NDR usage could concentrate around clock gates.
